name: Ragnell

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ragnell is an Arthurian heroine. After an enchantment turned her into a loathly lady, a cailleach or hag, she kept her sweet humor and good nature. She helped Gawain, a knight of the Round Table, find the answer to the riddle of what women truly want. Despite her uncomely looks, the fine knight fell in love with the wise and kind Ragnell. When they married she offered to be lovely by day and a hag by night, or the reverse, and asked which he preferred. When he let her choose for herself, the enchantment lifted. She became a beautiful young woman, showing that women want to make their own choices. Ragnell may be a form of the goddess of sovereignty. Her tale became the basis for Chaucer's Wife of Bath's Tale in the Canterbury Tales.
